inherited_claims: CausalChat combines optional CPDAG discovery, GPT-4 suggestions, graph editing and SEM coefficient updates, with visual summaries linked to responses.
Prompts ask for 1-to-4 causal-significance ratings, confounders, mediators and actionable latent-factor proposals.
The nonexpert study uses six university students and a fixed sequence of BIC feedback, LLM text and CausalChat Lite; reported edge errors are 5/18, 7/18 and 1/18 respectively.
Expert feedback explicitly raises missing citations and uncertainty about the quality of the model-provided scientific evidence.
inherited_identity.supported_claims_here: PDF pp. 10-12; citations concern, six students, fixed stages, self-selected edges and 5/18,7/18,1/18 counts

supported_claims_here: Three expert sessions and concerns about citations are qualitative evidence, not causal adoption effects.
Six students used fixed stages and selected edges; edge-editing means3.3 and0.9 minutes do not establish a bank productivity effect.

inherited_claims: CausalDS provides narrated synthetic SCM scenes, data files, a separate observation model and private scoring artifacts.
Interventional and counterfactual targets have separate identification decisions, with abstention on nonidentifiable tasks.
The paper reports a 100-scene exam sampled from 953 scenes and finds that symbolic success, interval quality, abstention and cost can diverge.

inspected_anchors: PDF pp. 2-3, 8-9; accessible corpora, synthetic exposure and generated contexts; scope of claims
inherited_claims: The study compares relation mentions in accessible OLMo/BLOOM pretraining corpora with pairwise causal judgments, and varies synthetic relation frequencies.
Reported relation frequency is positively associated with performance; reversed or negated mentions can reduce affirmative response frequency.
The context study uses GPT-4o-generated positive/negative contexts and human annotation; affirmative response rates vary substantially with context.
inherited_identity.supported_claims_here: PDF pp. 2-3, 8-9; accessible corpora, synthetic exposure and generated contexts; scope of claims

supported_claims_here: The study does not identify an error law for all closed models or complex dynamic banking tasks.

limitations: Author proposal development and exact project planning constructions; no measured bank ROI.
All new costs, losses, populations, state probabilities and pilot quality are stipulated.
Conditional probabilities are not inferred from language-model confidence or repeated agreement.
Published usability and benchmark evidence retains its original task, population and protocol limits.
No new model calls, external package execution, bank sample or implemented decision policy.
Authentic deployment weights, prices, assignments and owner acceptance are conditional later inputs.
Current manuscript depth is reviewed separately; rendered visual acceptance remains open.
